Expectation1: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation1: You get a frantic call from your friend whose car has broken down on the side of the highway late at night, and they need you to come get them immediately.
Expectation2: Attend weekly church services to worship and participate in community activities
Situation2: They think about joining Sunday worship when time allows
Story: It was almost midnight when my phone buzzed, jolting me from the edge of sleep. My friend’s voice trembled on the other end—her car had broken down on the highway, and she was scared, stranded in the dark. She begged me to come get her, and I could hear the desperation in her voice. I glanced at the clock. If I left now, I’d barely make it back in time for Sunday worship, something I’d promised myself I wouldn’t miss again. Church was more than a routine; it was my anchor, my way of connecting with God and my community. But my friend needed me, and I knew she had no one else to call. The weight of both expectations pressed on me—my loyalty as a friend, my commitment as a Christian. My heart pounded as I stared at my car keys, torn between the road to my friend and the path to the church.
